novum_candidates.description:
A storyworld in which ordinary household articles
described as sentient beings possess sentience, speech, gender, romantic desire, and social class distinctions, governing the entire narrative from the false collar's courtships through its transformation into the very paper the story is printed on.

novelty.rationale: The story presents a totalizing departure from the empirical norm: inanimate objects (a false collar, garter, box-iron, scissors, hair-comb) think, speak, court, marry, and are transformed into paper. This animation is not incidental but constitutes the entire fictive universe, differing wholly from the author's empirical reality.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The animation of the objects is offered without any immanent, systematic, nonsupernatural account. It operates by fairy-tale/fable convention (magical animism) rather than an imaginary science or coherent social-material logic. There is no explanatory mechanism; the sentience is simply asserted, placing this in the marvellous rather than the cognitively estranged mode.

narrative_hegemony.rationale:
The sentience of the objects is the overriding narrative logic. Every plot event
courtship, rejection, cutting, transformation into paper, and the closing moral addressed to the reader
depends entirely on the objects being animate. Nothing in the story exists apart from this conceit.

novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: Reader-facing contrast is created by the direct address comparing the reader's fate to the collar's (sfev-85edf0825198a599), and by the recursive conceit that the paper we read is the transformed collar (sfev-7ecefb05ecd73ac0). Storyworld consequences follow from the objects' animate agency (sfev-3368b4e61d273d6c). Character reactions such as the garter's indignation and the scissors cutting the collar are recorded separately as estrangement evidence and are not treated as required.
